verdict.rationale: a-Shell provides its own Apple Shortcuts actions. `Execute Command` runs a list of commands or a file, and `Put File`/`Get File` move data in and out, so the shell can be scripted without typing at the prompt. Shortcuts can also be forced to run "in Extension" rather than in the app, which approximates headless execution, though the docs warn this won't always work. missing for 10: a documented headless mode with no UI, CI/server-side runner integration, and independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: You can write complex Shortcuts to download, process and release files using a-Shell commands.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order. The input can also be a file or a text node
You can force a specific shortcut to run "in App" or "in Extension", with the warning that it won't always work.
